turns.text: /builder:init
⏺ Skill(builder:init) · Bash(git rev-parse --show-toplevel · ls .claude/builder.md · cat pnpm-workspace.yaml apps/*/package.json .github/workflows/ci.yml …)

Read the repo. Here's what it already told me:

- **project** `acme-certs` (root package.json) · **base** `main` (origin/HEAD) · **registry** `docs/features` (template default — no feature folder yet)
- **apps** from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: `api` (apps/api — Fastify + Prisma), `web` (apps/web — React + Vite), `mobile` (apps/mobile — React Native, `released_artifact: true`: it ships through the stores)
- **fast gates** from each package.json: `pnpm -F api test` · `pnpm -F api typecheck` · `pnpm -F web test` · `pnpm -F web lint`
- **walk readiness** from Prisma: `pnpm -F api prisma migrate status` / `deploy` / `generate`; dev start `pnpm dev`
- **ticket keys** like `ACME-207` in branch names and commit subjects → Jira
- no design resolver → prototype mode stays off

One thing to know before the agent questions: with agent mode on, **"go" at a build hands the feature to agents** — they build it, an agent tries it in the running app, and it is merged into `main` on this machine marked *not human-tested*. Nothing is pushed and no PR is opened. To test a feature yourself, pick **In this session** on its hand-off.

A few things only you can answer. Two in plain words:

1. **Known-red gates** — do any of the four gates above fail on `main` today?
2. **Flaky tests** — any test file that fails in the whole suite but passes alone?

The rest in the picker, my recommendation first on each.

turns.question: Is api the producer and web and mobile its consumers?

options.label: api → web, mobile (Recommended)
options.description: api owns the Prisma schema and serves the routes; web and mobile code against its contract. Phases run api first.

options.label: All three independent
options.description: No producer/consumer order — each app phases on its own and no contract freezes between them.

turns.question: Commit mode per app — may an agent commit, or only stage?

options.label: All auto (Recommended)
options.description: Agents commit in every app as each task lands.

options.label: mobile manual, rest auto
options.description: api and web commit as they go; in mobile an agent stages its changes and stops — that commit is yours.

options.label: All manual
options.description: Every app stages and stops; you make every commit.

turns.question: When a build adds a migration, how should it reach your dev database?

options.label: ask (Recommended)
options.description: The pipeline asks before applying a pending migration, so a walk never runs against an old schema.

options.label: agent
options.description: Applied without asking when it is additive; one that drops or rewrites data still asks.

options.label: human
options.description: Never applied for you — the pipeline names the command and waits.

turns.question: How should agents drive the app when they walk a feature (the agent_walk block — always written; it is what turns agent mode on)?

options.label: Playwright MCP (Recommended)
options.description: web already depends on playwright; agents click through the web app in a headless browser, in a walk env of its own (other ports, its own database).

options.label: Playwright scripts
options.description: agents write throwaway Playwright scripts instead of using the MCP tools — slower to author, but no MCP server to load.

options.label: API checks only
options.description: no browser; agents walk API items with curl and leave UI items for your walk — agent mode still on, but most features wait for you.

turns.question: Ticket keys like ACME-207 appear in branches and commits — write a Jira ticket block?

options.label: Jira, key ACME (Recommended)
options.description: Specs and branches carry the ticket key; builder reads tickets but never writes to Jira.

options.label: No ticket block
options.description: Ticket ids are never asked for or checked.

turns.text: Asked in one message: the two free-text questions in chat, the choices as AskUserQuestion (the tool takes up to four per call).
None red, no flaky ones. Roles yes, mobile manual, ask, Playwright MCP, Jira.

Naming this **bulk-renew**, from the ticket's title "Bulk renew certificates" — say if you want another name.

⚠ You're on `main`, which doesn't carry ACME-388 in its name.

**What ACME-388 asks for:** owners renewing certificates one at a time is the slow part of their year-end — the ticket wants them to "tick any number of certificates on the list and renew them in one go", with a shortcut to "renew everything expiring in the next 30 days". Each renewal "extends the certificate 12 months from today", a run is "capped at 500 certificates", and "mobile is out of scope for this ticket". It also says the list "already supports multi-select" and that renewals are "linked to the certificate they replace".

I pulled **15 claims** out of it — 6 requirements, 4 decisions, 2 constraints, 1 non-goal and 2 claims about how the code works today.

B. Let's correct it — tell me what the playback gets wrong before I check

turns.text: go
⏺ 4 Explore agents (sonnet) — verifying 15 claims against apps/api and apps/web

**12 of 15 claims confirmed · 2 contradicted · 1 unverifiable · 4 gaps**

**Confirmed**
- single renew exists — `POST /certificates/:id/renew` (apps/api/src/routes/certificates.ts:88)
- only the owner may renew — `assertOwner` guards it (apps/api/src/certificates/renew.service.ts:14)
- renewal sets `status: active` and writes a `renewed` event (renew.service.ts:36, :42)
- the list already filters by expiry window — `?expiresWithin=30` (apps/web/src/features/certificates/useCertificates.ts:21)
- mobile reads `expires_at` from the same list endpoint and needs no change (apps/mobile/src/api/certificates.ts:12)
- …and 7 more, each with its `file:line` in the record

**Contradicted**
- "renewal extends 12 months from today" — the code extends 12 months from the **current** `expires_at` (renew.service.ts:31)
- "the list already supports multi-select" — `CertificateTable` has no selection; the only checkbox column is in `AdminUsersTable` (apps/web/src/features/certificates/CertificateTable.tsx:18)

**Unverifiable**
- "500 renewals finish in under 2 seconds" — only running it against real data can say

**Gaps the ticket never decides** — a revoked or already-expired certificate in the selection · a run where some renewals fail · one history event per certificate or one for the batch (the History tab reads `/certificates/:id/events`) · what the "renew expiring" shortcut does when nothing is expiring

**How it works today:** renewing is one certificate at a time from the owner view — `renewCertificate` checks ownership, adds 12 months to the current expiry, sets the status back to active and records a `renewed` event[^1]. Nothing links a renewal to the certificate it replaced — the row is updated in place[^2].

[^1]: apps/api/src/certificates/renew.service.ts:14–42
[^2]: apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:41 — no `renewed_from_id`

---

**Q1 of ~7 — where a renewal's new expiry starts**

The ticket says 12 months from today; single renew runs 12 months from the current expiry. Which side changes?

**Why it matters:** renewing early either keeps or throws away the unexpired time — and if bulk and single renew disagree, two certificates renewed the same afternoon get different dates.
**What it affects:** `renewCertificate` (renew.service.ts:31), the Renew button on the owner view, the new bulk endpoint, the expiry dates web and mobile show.
**Your options:**
- **Keep the code's rule (Recommended)** — bulk renew extends from the current `expires_at`, exactly like single renew; the ticket's line is corrected in the spec. Early renewals keep their unexpired time.
- **Change code to the ticket's** — single and bulk renew both run 12 months from today. `renew.service.ts` changes, and anyone renewing early loses the time they had left.
- **Today, for bulk only** — bulk uses today, single keeps its rule. Two rules for one action, which the spec has to explain.

**Why Keep the code's rule:** single renew has extended from the current expiry since ACME-207 (`git log -S addMonths`), so bulk matches it and nobody loses paid-for time. It costs nothing in code; you give up the ticket's wording, which the spec corrects.

**Here's the shared understanding** — 2 parts. Owners renew many certificates in one action on the web.

**Part 1 of 2 — What users get**

**What changes for users**
- Before: an owner renews certificates one at a time from each owner view — the slow part of their year-end.
- After: an owner ticks certificates on the web list, or takes *Renew expiring in 30 days*, and renews them all in one action. Each renewal extends from its current expiry, exactly like single renew.
- Who: owners on the web. Mobile is untouched — it shows the new expiry dates as it does today.

**What they'll see**
```
┌ Certificates ─────────────────────────────── [Renew expiring in 30 days] ┐
│ [✓] Boiler 3 — gas safety        expires 12 Nov                        │
│ [✓] Lift 2 — LOLER               expires 19 Nov                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 2 selected                                     [Renew 2]  [Clear]       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
- After the run: "Renewed 41 · skipped 1 revoked · 0 failed", with the skipped ones named.

**Added · Changed · Removed**
- Added: selection on the certificate list · the selection bar · *Renew expiring in 30 days* · a bulk renew endpoint in api
- Changed: nothing about single renew
- Removed: nothing

A. Looks right — next part
B. Change something — say what
Reply A or B — "go" is A.
a

**Part 2 of 2 — Decisions and risks**

**Decisions**
- A renewal extends 12 months from the current expiry — *you*, keeping the code's rule — not "from today" as the ticket said, which throws away time owners paid for.
- The list gains its own selection — the ticket said it had one; it doesn't — built on the design system's `Checkbox` column.
- Revoked certificates in a selection are skipped and named, never renewed — *you*.
- A run where some renewals fail renews the rest and reports the failures — *you* — not all-or-nothing.
- One `renewed` event per certificate, so each History tab shows its own renewal — `renewCertificate` already writes it (renew.service.ts:42) *(assumed)*
- The 500 cap is enforced by both the endpoint and the selection bar — the web pattern for capped actions (ExportBar.tsx:30) *(assumed)*
- Confirmed as the ticket states them: owners only · status back to active · the 30-day window · mobile out of scope · …and 9 more, each with its evidence in the record.

**Risks and open questions**
- "500 renewals in under 2 seconds" couldn't be checked without real data — the build times it.

**Not included** — mobile; renewing for anything but 12 months; undoing a bulk renewal.

B. Park it — keep the conversation; nothing is built
C. Stop here — the understanding is the outcome; nothing written to the repo

stages.when: After the user confirms the understanding and picks Build it.

turns.text: A

**Size: lg** — evidence: two apps (api: a new `POST /certificates/bulk-renew` endpoint and its contract row; web: selection on the certificate list, a selection bar, a confirm dialog and a results summary); mobile ⬜ — it reads `expires_at` already. Rule 4: two apps → lg.

**Split it?**

One spec, or two that each ship on their own?

**Why it matters:** each spec is its own build, walk and merge — two means two walks, but the first lands sooner.
**What it affects:** the order api and web phases run in, and when owners get anything.
**Your options:**
- **One spec (Recommended)** — bulk-renew as one lg spec: the endpoint, selection and the "renew expiring" shortcut together. One build, one walk.
- **2 value-sized specs** — bulk-renew-selected (owners tick and renew) first, bulk-renew-expiring (the 30-day shortcut) after. Each usable on its own; the first lands sooner, at the cost of a second walk.

**Why One spec:** the shortcut is one button over the same endpoint, so splitting it off saves little and costs a second walk. You give up landing the selection a little sooner.

**Testing while building — your options:**
- **Its own tests (Recommended)** — quick: one small run per slice, the tests that slice adds and the type-check.
- **Its own, plus the app's suite when the app's slices are done** — adds one suite run per app, once its slices are done.
- **The app's suite after every slice** — slowest: a suite run per slice; catches a break where it happened.
- **None while building** — fastest: the type-check only; tests are written but run at the end.

**Testing at the end — your options:**
- **The touched apps' suites, once (Recommended)** — one suite run per app: the fast set, the tests §Testing names, released-consumer parity.
- **Plus an agent tries the risky parts** — adds an agent walking the [risk] items in the running app.
- **Everything** — slowest: the deep set, the cross-app E2E, the full walk.
- **Nothing — I'll test it** — fastest: the type-check only; the verdict says nothing was tested.

**Review — your options:**
- **Once at the end (Recommended)** — one whole-branch review.
- **Once per app** — one after each app's slices.
- **After every slice** — one per slice.

**Why the recommended levers:** cert-history touches only web and adds no migration, so its own tests per slice and the web suite once cover it. You give up an agent trying it in the running app.

sources: skills/help/SKILL.md §The go-ahead and the test plan

turns.text: /builder:help
⏺ Skill(builder:help)

# `/builder:*` — how builder works

## In one paragraph

You say what you want with `/builder:brainstorm`. It looks up what your words refer to in the code,
explains how that part works today, asks only what is still open, and — once you agree on what to
build — sizes it. A small change is built right there in the chat. A bigger one gets a written spec
you approve; it is checked against the code once, planned, built one app at a time, tested, and
merged. By default agents build and test it and merge it on your machine, marked *not human-tested*;
you can test it yourself instead, and then nothing becomes a PR until you sign off.

## Setup

Everything builder knows about your project lives in one file, **`.claude/builder.md`**: your apps,
their test commands, your house rules. `/builder:init` writes it from what the repo contains and
asks only what it can't tell; `/builder:init --update` fills gaps in an existing one. If a step says
it can't find the config, that file is what's missing. Nothing else needs installing.

## Which command do I run?

| You want to… | Run |
|---|---|
| **Start anything** — explore an idea, ask for a change, think something through | `/builder:brainstorm <what you want>` |
| **Build from a spec, brief or ticket someone already wrote** | `/builder:intake <file · ticket · pasted doc>` — checks every claim against the code and asks only about what's contradicted or missing |
| **See everything in progress** | `/builder:status` — one table, with the next step for each |
| **Pick up where you left off** | `/builder:resume` — no argument lists everything in flight |
| **Hand unfinished work to agents** | `/builder:agent` — tick features from a list; agents finish each and merge it. Every hand-off where agents could take over offers it as **1. Agent**, except the plan go-ahead, which launches agents itself |
| **Build several specs while you're away** | `/builder:fleet <features…>` |
| **Build it yourself in this session** | pick **In this session** on a hand-off before the build (or `/builder:resume --path <folder> --here`) — it is planned and built here, then stops for you to try it |
| **Record that you tried it and it works** | `/builder:signoff --path <folder> <your words>` — only you can type it; `--hold "<reason>"` means "works, don't push yet" |
| **Change a feature that's already planned or part-built** | `/builder:revise --path <folder> <the change>` |
| **Clean up leftover branches and worktrees** | `/builder:tidy` |
| **Clear finished specs out of the way** | `/builder:archive` — shipped, merged and abandoned folders move into `_archive/`, each kept as its SPEC |
| **Build from a finished design** | `/builder:check --<design.flag> <ref>` to see if it's ready, then `/builder:intake --<design.flag> <ref>` — the flag's name comes from your config |
| **Update builder, or see which one you're on** | `/builder:update` · `/builder:version` (a copy inside the repo updates with `/builder:vendor`) |
| **Watch it run** | `/builder:statusline` — a live builder progress bar; `--off` removes it |

The steps `/builder:resume` runs for you can also be run by hand, each with `--path <folder>`:
`/builder:spec`, `/builder:audit`, `/builder:plan`, `/builder:build`, `/builder:verify`,
`/builder:ship`. Flags come first and the free text after them is the request.

## What happens to a feature

**Size.** Decided once you agree on what to build, with the reason; you can override it, and it only
ever goes up.
- **xs / sm** — stays inside existing code and one app, including a new command or endpoint only
  that app uses. Designed and built in the chat; nothing is written under `docs/`.
- **md / lg** — adds a model, a schema field, a permission or a screen, an endpoint another app
  calls, or crosses from one app into another. Gets `SPEC.md` and a ~12-line `MANIFEST.md`.
- **xl** — split into several features under one `PROGRAM.md`.
- "Can we…?" is answered as a question, not turned into a feature.

**Order (md and lg):**

```
spec → audit (once) → open questions → plan → go-ahead → build (one app at a time)
     → tested → verify (the one deep check) → merged, or a PR after your sign-off
```

**Who tests it.** After you approve the spec the hand-off offers:
1. **Agent** — "go" picks it. Agents plan, build, try it in the running app, verify, and merge it
   into your main branch on your machine (`merge_into` picks another), recorded as
   `🤖 AGENT SIGNED OFF — not human-tested`. Nothing is pushed; no PR.
2. **Step by step** — the same, pausing for you at the open questions and the plan's go-ahead.
3. **In this session** — built here, then 🔒 it stops for **your walk**: you try it in the running
   app and type `/builder:signoff`. Only then come verify and **one PR for the whole feature**. A
   plugin hook blocks `gh pr create` until you have signed off.

**Several apps in one repo.** Each app gets its own phase, the one that provides an API before the
ones that use it, and each phase runs that app's own tests. The shared contract between apps freezes
once the providing app's phase passes; only `/builder:revise` reopens it, and it names every app to
re-check. An app marked `commit: manual` is never committed by an agent.

## The go-ahead and the test plan

The plan is shown as numbered slices, grouped by app, each with the tests it adds, and a test plan
with what it costs. "go" takes the recommended one; *Change the test plan* asks:
- **Testing per slice** — its own tests (recommended) · plus the app's suite when its slices are
  done · the app's suite after every slice · none while building.
- **Testing at the end** — the touched apps' suites once (recommended) · plus an agent tries the
  risky parts · everything · nothing — you test it.
- **Review** — once at the end (recommended) · once per app · after every slice.

With the end set to the risky parts or everything, it also asks **Walk it yourself before it
lands?** — yes parks the agent build for your walk and lands it after your sign-off. A breaking
schema change, a migration or a released consumer raises the recommended end, and says why. **Two
floors hold under every plan:** a type-check of every touched app before the work lands, and one
final whole-branch review.

## Resuming

Each feature's `MANIFEST.md` says where it stands and what's next, and every step ends with:

```
📍 <feature>: <state> — next: <what happens next>
```

Reply **go** to continue, or pick a numbered option where there's more than one way on — "go" picks
1. After a `/clear`, `/builder:resume` (or just ask to continue). A few things wait for you on
purpose: your walk and sign-off, a step only you can do, a hold, and opening the PR, which asks
once. "go, but …" is a change, not a go.

## Words you'll see

**spec** `SPEC.md`, what and why, kept after it ships · **manifest** `MANIFEST.md`, where it stands ·
**plan** `PLAN.md`, the build step by step · **walk** trying it yourself in the running app ·
**sign-off** your verdict after the walk · **verify** the final full check · **park** stopped for
a decision only you can make, with what and why.

## FAQ

- **Where are the files?** `<registry>/<feature>/` — `SPEC.md`, `MANIFEST.md`, `PLAN.md`. When it
  ships, the folder shrinks to its `SPEC.md` and moves to `<registry>/_archive/`; git keeps the rest.
- **The audit found problems.** Normal — they become fixes in the spec. It runs once; anything still
  uncertain is carried into the build as a named risk.
- **My walk found problems.** They go in the spec's `## Fixes` list, each naming its app; they're
  fixed, you try again, and sign off.
- **A small change after the build?** Just fix the code. `/builder:revise` is for a change that
  unbuilt work depends on.
- **Does it need other plugins, update my tickets, deploy, or write my design system?** No. It
  never creates a ticket, pushes, or deploys.
- **What are its hooks?** Two, silent outside a repo with `.claude/builder.md`: a short brief at
  session start, and the PR lock. The guide (`docs/guide.md` in the plugin's repo) says how to turn
  them off.
- **How work is done.** Four skills set it, and every implementer gets them:
  `/builder:test-driven-development`, `/builder:systematic-debugging`,
  `/builder:receiving-code-review`, `/builder:verification-before-completion` — *no claim that
  something works without fresh evidence.*
The skill renders the parts relevant to what was asked; a bare /builder:help gets the whole card, shown here.
